criteria.retire_with_register: Once the wire legs go live, delete the runners and transcribe each check-blocked leg into a lasting coverage register kept in the checklist and the Can file headers: the check's name, the absent primitive, and the parking date. The 28 records close with declared gaps; the register replaces the runners as the home of uncovered checks.
criteria.runners_stay: Runners that cover check-blocked legs never retire: the .mjs/.ts files continue to execute those legs in CI or manually. Their companion Can files hold the migrated wire legs and the blocked-leg records. Migration success is tallied as 28 minus the explicitly parked records, with the parked set named as unmigrated.
criteria.substitute_narrow_property: Retirement demands a live Can verdict for every leg, but the verdict may target a stricter, smaller property that production behavior genuinely exhibits: exact emitted CSP directive text in place of browser-side blocking proof, exact set-cookie strings in place of jar-behavior proof. A check with no truthful narrowing keeps its runner under the runners-stay rule.

blocked_retirement.instructions: How should the migration treat whole checks that Can cannot run when it decides whether their runners may retire?

state.aspect_vs_check: Blocked comes in two strengths and they must not be confused. In aspect-blocked legs the property itself is established in Can by other means and a single facet stays dark: A01/A02/B04 establish caps and one-shot semantics through sequential runs while true simultaneity stays unproven, and those runners are already gone — settled precedent. In check-blocked legs nothing about the check is established in Can: 'Chromium emits a CSP violation' or 'the jar drops a forged __Host- cookie' cannot run anywhere in the language. This question covers check-blocked legs only.
state.blocked_inventory: The unexecutable set spans the C03 probe.ts browser finale (lines 227-277, 2 groups), roughly 5 of the 9 proof.mjs groups, and strict-redirect.mjs's form-action refusal plus click-driven cookie legs. Needed primitives: page-script execution with DOM, style, font, and media readback (getComputedStyle, fonts.ready, decoded dimensions, clicks), an authentic cookie store (__Host- scoping, HttpOnly, SameSite, carriage over redirects, forgery rejection), browser CSP trip signals (securitypolicyviolation), navigation carrying default or overridden referrers, and worker/serviceworker admission. Client-side TLS-listener proof is check-blocked (Bun fetch aborts on the self-signed fixtures, shown 2026-10-02); bind-only server legs remain live.
state.gate_text: The checklist gate states that a host harness disappears only after its kept legs succeed as executing Can verdicts over real production behavior, with F01 reconciling and only fulfilled obligations counted. The 28 records span 21 code files, 3 documents, and 4 more owned artifacts; C02 holds 2 .mjs runners, C03 holds 2 .ts probes and README.md, C04 holds 5 fixtures. S04 (approval_probe.ts) carries no browser legs and should retire cleanly.
state.mandate: The language is authored by AI agents with no debt to earlier artifacts, and project law favors reaching the goal over building scaffolding or proof tiers. An earlier Jev round (unanimous 3/3 at 0.96+ confidence, 2026-10-02), confirmed by the user, chose migrating every wire-visible leg with explicit blocked legs and no fresh runtime surface. This round fixes the fate of the blocked residue.
state.precedent_pressure: All twelve fulfilled records retired clean: no runner has yet been let go with a check-blocked leg outstanding (the harshest case so far is aspect-blocked simultaneity beside a sequentially proven property). C02/C03 are the first queues with wholly unexecutable checks, so the chosen rule writes the migration's completion standard for unportable coverage and will anchor F01.
